text: A property lets an attribute look like plain data, but secretly run code when you read or write it.
The at-property decorator turns celsius into a getter — you access it with no parentheses, like an attribute.
[chuckle] The matching setter runs whenever you assign to it, letting you validate the new value first.
Here the setter rejects any temperature below absolute zero, protecting your object from impossible data.
[sniff] Properties are also perfect for computed values that depend on other attributes.
fahrenheit isn't stored anywhere — it's calculated fresh from celsius every time you ask.
So reading t dot fahrenheit runs the conversion on the spot, always up to date.
[sigh] Assign a new celsius, and fahrenheit instantly reflects it, because it's recomputed from the source.
[groan] Properties give you the clean syntax of attributes with the safety and smarts of methods — the best of both.
